title: Strix Writer: tests and exercises for teachers
description: Strix Writer is an open-source editor for teachers, written in Rust: calculation exercises with live solutions and variants, multiple-choice and open questions with points, tests assembled from an archive, and scores tables that add up by themselves. Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD and the web.
socialAlt: Strix Writer: write the test, Strix keeps the solutions and the scores
heroTitle2: Strix keeps the solutions and the scores.
heroLead: Strix Writer is an editor for preparing tests. Calculation exercises keep their data, solution and results live, with a variant for each row of desks; multiple-choice and open questions carry their points; a scores table adds them up by itself.
heroNote: Free and open source (MIT or Apache-2.0) · Windows · macOS · Linux · FreeBSD · web · no account, no telemetry
shotCalcAlt: Strix with a physics calculation: a car accelerating from rest, its acceleration from the speeds in km/h and the time, the force, the distance with its solution steps and a check with a tick
stat1Text: of exercise: problem, open answer, multiple choice, true/false
stat2Text: variants of the data, each with its solution recalculated
stat3Text: a scores table by criterion that totals itself as you type
stat4Text: one file per exercise; tests are assembled from it without changing it
howTitle: From the first exercise to the scores, in one document.
a1Text: Data, solution and results calculate in the page, with units. Choose variant B and the data, the solution and the results summary follow: no solution to redo by hand.
a2Text: Problems, open answers with a space in cm, multiple choice and true/false in the same test. The correct boxes are ticked, and they hide with the solution while the layout stays the same.
a3Title: From the archive to the test
a3Text: One file per exercise makes an archive. A master document assembles the test with its own cover page and numbering, with or without the solutions, in a DSA version too, and never changes the files.
a4Title: The points add up by themselves
a4Text: Each question carries its points; the scores table totals them by criterion and by exercise as you type. A grading grid that turns points into marks is planned.
mathIntro: An equation typed with the equation editor is typeset like any other, and it is the calculation. Errors never stop the sheet: a failing statement shows ⚠ and its message, and the rest still calculates.
math1: Solving: the unknown is isolated symbolically when it appears once (powers, roots, exp, ln, trigonometry), found numerically otherwise.
math2: Units are typeset upright and coloured, converted to the working unit, with a hint for the wrong case (“did you mean kN?”).
math3: Solution steps: the formula solved for the unknown, the values substituted, the result, aligned at =.
math4: Calculated tables: headers name columns with units and formulas, Σ = totals them, every column becomes a vector.
math5: Sums, ranges and vectors: ∑, ∏, i = 1..5, [1; 2; 3] kN, with a number format by digits, decimals or significant figures.
mathFigureLabel: Solving, units and a calculated table in a Strix document
tableCaption: A calculated table: density measured in the lab, columns with units and a formula, the mean, every column a vector afterwards.
featTitle: Everything a test needs, on a real document editor
featIntro: What is in Strix today. Planned work is marked as planned.
f1Text: The solution’s equations calculate with units, and every variant of the data recalculates the solution and the results summary. Each exercise is a sandbox: two can both use <var>t</var>.
f2Title: Multiple choice, true/false and open answers
f2Text: Options A), B), C)… with check boxes, more than one correct if you like; answer spaces in cm, squared or blank; points beside each question.
f3Text: One file per exercise, with grade, subject, duration and score as properties; a master document makes the test.
f4Title: A scores table that totals itself
f4Text: Criteria you name (IMP, MOD, CAL…), points given and available, totals across and down.
f5Text: One = defines, shows, solves or checks; units are checked on every step; solution steps on request.
f6Title: The same test, for every student
f6Text: DSA versions that combine, white page always; squared paper after the questions, sharp at any zoom and in PDF.
f7Text: A triangle drawn from <var>b</var> and <var>h</var> redraws when the variant changes; dimensions show their values.
f8Text: Ribbon, styles, tables, comments, spelling, printing; saves .xmath, opens DOCX, ODT, RTF; exports PDF, LaTeX, HTML.
f9Title: Native on every desktop, and in the browser
f9Text: Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD as native apps, and the same app compiled to WebAssembly. The interface follows the system’s language (English, Italian, German or French) and its light or dark theme.
plannedText: A grading grid that turns points into marks (thresholds, scale, rounding); a results table per exercise and checks against expected values; an Archive pane and search across the archive; Variables pane, plots, matrices; CAD modify tools.
exTitle: Calculation exercises, multiple choice, tests and scores
exIntro: The Teaching tab holds everything a test needs. Exercises keep a structure that editing can’t break: you write freely inside it, and the skeleton stays.
ex1: Calculation exercises: statement, data, nested questions, the solution worked under each question and one results summary; variants A, B, C recalculate it all.
ex2: Multiple choice, true/false and open answers, each question with its points; the correct answers hide with the solution, the spaces keep their height.
ex3: Tests from an archive: a master document assembles one file per exercise, with its own cover page, numbering and parts shown, and leaves the files as they are.
ex4: A scores table with a row per exercise and two columns per criterion (points given, points available), totalled across and down.
ex5: DSA formatting of the same test (reading, writing, maths and memory) and PDF for printing. Planned: a grading grid from points to marks.
shotExerciseAlt: A Strix exercise: a car accelerating from rest, its data in two variants, lettered questions and the solution worked under each question
cadIntro: A CAD drawing sits in the text like a picture, but its coordinates can be expressions of the parameters defined above it. Change b = 8cm and the triangle redraws; its dimension reads the new value.
cad1: Labels from parameters: {{L}} shows 4.5 m, {{L:both}} shows L = 4.5 m, <> the measured size.
cad2: An editor on the drawing’s sheet: lines, circles, arcs, polylines, rectangles, texts and dimensions, with a command line for coordinates.
cad3: Exact snaps on the true curves (endpoint, midpoint, centre, intersection, perpendicular, tangent…) from a geometry kernel tested to 1e-9.
cad4: Grips reshape objects and keep the expressions: L becomes L + 0.5.
cad5: Properties and layers: colour, lineweight, linetype, and the geometry as numbers or expressions. Saved with an SVG picture, so other programs still show it.
cadFigureLabel: A parametric right triangle whose dimensions show b = 8 cm and h = 6 cm
cadCaption: The triangle’s corners are the expressions ["b", 0] and [0, "h"]: change b or h and the drawing and its dimensions follow.
agTitle: Built to be driven by people and by agents
agIntro: Everything Strix does is a command with an id and parameters. The ribbon, keyboard shortcuts, command search, the command line, a local control channel and the MCP server all run the same commands, and programmatic calls never open dialogs.
agNote: The control channel and the MCP server listen on 127.0.0.1 only and need a per-window key; an agent can be confined to chosen folders.
dlIntro: Installers and portable builds for every platform. Strix is in alpha: keep a copy of important documents, and tell us what breaks.
dlWindowsNote: Windows 10 and 11. The builds are not code-signed yet: SmartScreen may warn on first run. The portable exe needs no installation and keeps its settings in a StrixData folder beside it.
dlMacNote: One universal build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
dlLinuxNote: x86_64 and aarch64; riscv64 as deb, rpm and tar.gz.
dlBsdNote: The app and the command line, with licences and icons.
dlWebNote: The same app compiled to WebAssembly: nothing to install. The ZIP is a static site you can host yourself.
dlPickText: Every build is listed below, grouped by system. Not sure which? The browser version runs anywhere, with nothing to install.
dlArchGuess: The browser doesn’t say which processor this is: on an ARM computer, choose ARM64 (aarch64).
dlMobileTitle: Strix on a phone or tablet
dlMobileText: Strix is a desktop app for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD. On this device, use the browser version: the same app, nothing to install.
dlNoBuildTitle: No native build for this system yet
dlNoBuildText: Use the browser version, or build Strix from source (see below).
dlDmgHint: Apple silicon and Intel in one app
dlBsdTarHint: The app and the command line
dlWebZipHint: A static site to host yourself
t1Text: Strix sends nothing on its own: no usage data, no crash reports, no update check. Documents and preferences stay on your computer.
t2Text: Production code has no unwrap, expect or unsafe; every command is tested with hostile parameters, and recovery copies protect open documents.
t3Text: A .xmath file is a standard OOXML package. Exports to PDF, LaTeX, HTML and Markdown keep your work readable anywhere.
t4Text: MIT or Apache-2.0, developed in the open, with every bundled font, dictionary and translation attributed.
startTitle: Build it and open the sample
startIntro: You need a Rust toolchain (1.95 or later); the web build also needs Trunk and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target.
startWeb: Or run it in the browser
startThen: Then open the Math tab, choose New Calculation, type L = 4.5 m and keep going. Design notes:
